item.description:
Lectern 1.6.0

Summary Studio with fact-checked summaries, study modes, past papers, Listen, semantic search, quick capture and references

This is the "1.2.0" feature release. It's numbered 1.6.0 because Lectern 1.5.3 is already installed and updates can only go forward.

Added

  • **Summary Studio** (wand button on every page, ⇧⌘S): 17 formats (bullets, numbered, checklist, outline, paragraphs, Cornell, three table styles, Q&A, glossary, mind map, timeline, flowchart, one-page cheat sheet, TL;DR, slide by slide, formula sheet, layered, custom); lengths from TL;DR to comprehensive or a word count, with a word and reading-time estimate; level, focus areas and keywords; include/exclude citations, examples, formulas, diagrams, "things to clarify" and exam questions; output language with bilingual key terms; six built-in presets plus your own, with defaults per subject and page type; insert into the page's Summary section, at the cursor, as a new page or to the clipboard.
  • A new fact-based summary engine: facts first (cached by file and settings, so changing format or length is quick), then writing, then every statement checked against its slides. Unconfirmed statements are marked "⚠ check" with the source on hover. Coverage is checked per slide (per topic for short summaries) and a report line shows slides covered, topics, statements verified, the model and the time. Prompts live in editable files with worked examples; temperatures are 0.2 for facts and checks and 0.5 for writing; small models get smaller sections and topic-by-topic writing.
  • Layered summaries (TL;DR, then key points that expand, then slide references), "Summarise together" for several pages with citations like [Slides 12] [Reading p. 4] [Recording 14:32], and week, topic and subject summaries built from page summaries.
  • Mind maps, timelines and flowcharts drawn by Lectern, with zoom, PNG/SVG export and "Edit as Outline".
  • Per-section tools (Regenerate, Shorter, Longer, Simpler, More examples, Change format, Verify again), format changes without AI for lists and tables, 👍/👎 ratings that adjust your defaults, and summary version history with side-by-side compare and restore.
  • **Summarise All…** and a **Processing Queue** window: progress and time left, pause, resume, cancel, drag to reorder, carries on after a restart, can wait until the Mac is plugged in and idle, and notifies you when done.
  • Better reading of files: titles, headings, nesting and reading order (including two-column PDFs), tables from PDF, PowerPoint and Word, speaker notes, formulas as maths, on-device OCR with automatic language detection and a confidence note, and topic detection. Clean-up removes repeated headers and footers, slide numbers, copyright lines, "Questions?"/"Thank you"/agenda/blank slides and build-up duplicates, and joins "(cont.)" slides, with a "Cleaned: removed N…" note you can open.
  • New sources: .srt and .vtt captions, transcripts with timestamps, recordings matched to slides, EPUB books by chapter, images and handwriting by OCR, and web articles with their title, author and date.
  • **Active recall** (key terms blurred; the ones you didn't know become flashcards), **blurting** (timed, typed or dictated, then compared with your notes and scored) and **Feynman mode** (explain to a curious AI student, then get a clarity score). A **Daily Review** on Home: due cards, five quick questions and one blurt, with settings for length and mix.
  • **Past papers**: import PDFs or scans, questions and marks are found and linked to your lectures; practise one at a time or as a timed mock, marked against your lectures and any official solution. Likely exam topics, and a readiness score per subject with your five weakest topics and a one-click Planner plan.
  • **Listen** (⌥⌘L): pages read aloud with the best installed voice, play/pause, 0.75–2× speed, skip by section, current sentence highlighted, maths read naturally; export a page or a week's summaries as an M4A audio file with chapters.
  • **Semantic search** with an Ollama embedding model (background indexing, keyword and meaning results combined); "Ask about this subject" uses it with citations; **smart folders** (saved searches) and an interactive **graph** of linked pages in the sidebar.
  • **Quick capture** from anywhere (⌃⌥Space): note, paste, link or screenshot (its text is read with OCR), with subject and tags; **Services → Send to Lectern**; an **Inbox** with "Suggest where this belongs".
  • **References**: look up DOIs (Crossref) and ISBNs (Open Library); APA 7, Harvard (AGPS), MLA 9, Chicago and IEEE; copy references and in-text citations; lists per subject or assessment as text, rich text or BibTeX.
  • **Reading mode** (⌥⌘R): line width, line, letter and word spacing, a reading ruler and the dyslexia-friendly OpenDyslexic font (SIL Open Font License, included).
  • Templates gallery with Weekly Review, Lab Report Planner, Essay Planner and Group Meeting Notes, and "Save as Template…" for any page.
  • Daily backups (keeps 14, in a folder you choose) with restore of one page or everything; detection of sync conflict copies with a side-by-side merge.
  • Model routing per task (facts, writing, checking, flashcards, chat, embeddings) with an "Auto" choice that picks the best installed model and falls back to Claude within your monthly limit.

Changed

  • Tests never read the Keychain.

Fixed

  • PDF text no longer loses letters or splits words on some slides.

Lectern 1.5.3

Flashcards show which slide or page they came from

Added

  • New flashcards show which slide or page their information came from ("From Slide 7", or "Page 3 · Article" for notes from a link or file), checked against your notes. Click it to open that slide beside your notes, or the link or file. Shown when cards are created, in the page's flashcards panel, while studying, in decks and in the page's Flashcards section. Cards made from highlighted text get their slide too.

Lectern 1.5.2

Flashcards on a page are now real flip cards with Previous and Next

Added

  • A page's flashcards now appear as real cards in the side panel: click to flip, with Previous and Next underneath and a card counter. ← → and Space work after clicking the card. A Cards / List switch keeps the list view.
